This rests on the (completely false) premise that AI is doing anything other than simply parroting our human knowledge back at us

It has no capacity to think, argue, demonstrate, or certainly do anything even remotely close to “intelligence”

young_mete · Oct 10, 2026

It doesn't assume, it just observes. It has the capacity to use computers better than us, more persistently, in a more scalable way, to solve problems we haven't solved before like Navier-Stokes and many more to come. You can argue all you want about whether it's intelligent or not and what it means, but the solution is now here for us to process, understand, and integrate forward into our model of the world.

asimpletune · Oct 10, 2026

> All this new knowledge is arriving at a pace much greater than the field’s ability to process it

That’s the whole issue: it’s not knowledge, it’s data. AI can not provide an account for the proofs, or be questioned about them, or organize a talk exposing the idea because there’s no understanding behind any of it.

This is what Tao has been saying; that the results, in the strictest sense, were never the goal. It is ultimately the understanding (that previously was required to form a proof) that is valuable.

young_mete · Oct 10, 2026

Fair, “answers” is probably more precise than “knowledge.” That gap between answers and understanding is the whole point of the post, so I think we mostly agree.
